title: It is finished (John 19:25–30)
hookLine: his mother, the beloved disciple, I thirst, and it is finished
carry: a debt paid, a victory won

lines: A FEW STAYED NEAR THE CROSS.
cards: While the soldiers gamble, a few people stand near the cross. John names them. His mother.
His mother's sister. Mary the wife of Cleophas. Mary Magdalene.
And the disciple whom Jesus loved. The other men who followed him are nowhere in John's scene. These few stayed.
And from the cross, with the little breath he has left, Jesus speaks to them. In John's Gospel, he says only three things from the cross.

teach.b: The first is to his mother and his friend. In the King James Bible: "Woman, behold thy son!" And to the disciple: "Behold thy mother!"
From that hour, John says, that disciple took her to his own home. Dying, he makes sure his mother has a home. Christians read it in more than one way.
Read plainly, it's simple, faithful care. Catholic and Orthodox Christians also hear Mary given as mother to the church, with the beloved disciple standing for every follower.
The second: "I thirst." The man who offered a woman at a well living water, and said whoever believes in him will never thirst, is thirsty.
Someone lifts a sponge of sour wine to him on a branch of hyssop, the plant used at the first Passover to mark the doorposts. Then the third.
"When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost." In Greek, it is finished is one word: tetelestai.
It comes from telos, the end, the goal, the point something has been moving toward. It doesn't mean it's over, I'm done for.
It means complete, accomplished, brought to its goal. Just before, John uses the same verb: Jesus, knowing that all things were now accomplished.
Christians hear this one word as the heart of what they believe the cross achieved, and churches describe that in different words: a debt paid, a victory won, love shown to the end.
Each reading hears completion, not defeat.
John makes it sound like a choice. He handed over his spirit.

how: On Good Friday many churches hold services around Jesus's last words from the cross, sometimes called the Seven Last Words, gathered from all four Gospels; three of them come from John.

o: it is over, and I am done for
it is too late to turn back now
it is complete, brought to its goal

games.q: what's inside John 19:25–30 — tap the pairs.

s: tetelestai means complete, accomplished, brought to its goal.
in John, Jesus speaks three times from the cross
to his mother and friend, 'I thirst', and 'it is finished'.
all of Jesus's male disciples stood at the cross
John names women, and one disciple: the one Jesus loved.

games.q: you're dying, and your mother is standing below with your closest friend. what do you say?
o: woman, behold thy son. and to him: behold thy mother.
games.why: he gives them to each other, and from that hour the disciple took her to his own home.

practice: Think of one small thing you've left half done, a text never sent, a drawer half sorted, a thank-you note, and picture yourself completing it and then stopping: not grabbing the next thing, just resting in done.
If you pray, offer that small completion to God; if not, simply notice how good finished feels.

wordCard.voice: Tetelestai. One word in Greek for it is finished: not it's over, but it's complete, brought to its goal.

orig.note: Greek: it is finished, it stands complete. from telos, the end or goal. one word in Greek.

carryVoice: Your line: a debt paid, a victory won. Or, as others say it, love shown to the end. See you tomorrow.
